resources.string: Setup
Execution
Instructions for this exercise are not available in this version. Follow your own setup and technique, and use a load you can control.
Close
Lie on the bench with your eyes beneath the bar. Plant both feet, settle your upper back on the pad, and take an even grip just wider than shoulder width. Unrack the bar with your arms extended.

Lower the bar under control toward the middle of your chest, keeping your wrists over your elbows. Touch lightly without bouncing, then press up until your arms are extended. Keep your shoulders settled against the bench.

Sit on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, then lie back and hold them beside your chest. Plant both feet and keep your upper back supported. Turn your palms forward or slightly inward, whichever feels comfortable.

Press both dumbbells upward over your chest without letting them collide. Lower them under control until your elbows are beside or slightly below your torso, within a comfortable range. Keep both sides moving smoothly.

Place your hands on the floor a little wider than shoulder width and extend your legs behind you. Brace your trunk so your head, hips and legs form a steady line. Use an elevated hand support if needed to make the movement manageable.

Bend your elbows and lower your chest between your hands while keeping your body in one line. Stop at a comfortable depth, then press the floor away to return to the start. Avoid letting your hips sag or rise ahead of your shoulders.
Stand with the bar at your upper chest and take a balanced grip just outside your shoulders. Set your feet comfortably, keep your trunk steady, and position your elbows slightly in front of the bar.

Press the bar overhead in a controlled path, moving your head clear as the bar passes. Finish with the bar balanced over your shoulders and feet, without forcing your lower back to arch. Lower it smoothly to your upper chest.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and support yourself with the other hand on a stable bench or surface. Set your feet securely and keep your back steady, with the working arm hanging below your shoulder.

Draw the dumbbell toward your hip, keeping your elbow close to your side. Pause briefly without twisting your torso, then lower the weight until your arm is extended. Complete the repetitions on one side before switching.

Sit facing the cable station and secure your thighs beneath the pads. Take the bar with an even, comfortable overhand grip. Sit tall and let your arms extend overhead without losing a steady torso position.

Pull the bar down toward your upper chest while keeping your torso mostly upright and your elbows moving down. Return the bar overhead slowly until your arms extend comfortably. Do not swing or pull the bar behind your neck.
Sit facing the cable station with feet on the supports and knees slightly bent. Take the handle with both hands and sit tall, allowing your arms to reach forward while keeping your torso steady.

Draw the handle toward your lower ribs, moving your elbows back without leaning to create momentum. Briefly settle your shoulder blades, then let the cable carry your hands forward under control while maintaining your seated position.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand beside your thighs. Keep a soft bend in your elbows and choose a load you can lift without swinging. Set your feet comfortably and keep your torso steady.

Raise your arms out to the sides in a smooth arc, leading with your elbows. Stop around shoulder height or sooner if that is your comfortable range. Lower the dumbbells slowly; avoid shrugging or using momentum.

Set the bar securely across your upper back and take an even grip. Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart, or in a stance that lets you squat comfortably. Brace your trunk and make sure the bar is stable before stepping back.

Bend your hips and knees together, keeping your whole foot in contact with the floor. Descend only as far as you can maintain a steady position, then stand by pushing through the floor. Keep the bar balanced over your mid-foot.

Hold one dumbbell vertically close to your chest with both hands supporting it. Stand with your feet in a comfortable squat stance and brace your trunk. Keep the weight close rather than letting your arms drift forward.

Bend your hips and knees to lower between your legs while keeping the weight close to your chest. Use a depth where your balance and torso remain controlled, then stand smoothly. Keep your feet grounded throughout.
Stand with a barbell held in front of your thighs and feet about hip width apart. Keep your knees softly bent, arms long and trunk braced. Begin with the bar close to your body.

Push your hips back and let the bar slide close down your thighs and shins. Keep your back steady and knees softly bent; stop when your hamstrings limit the hinge or your position would change. Drive your hips forward to stand tall without leaning back.

Adjust the machine so its pivot is near your knee and the roller rests comfortably against the backs of your lower legs. Set the seat and supports, then hold the handles with your hips supported against the pad.

Bend your knees to draw the roller through a comfortable range without lifting your hips. Pause briefly, then extend your legs slowly until they return to the starting position. Keep the movement smooth rather than letting the stack drop.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms by your sides and palms facing forward or slightly inward. Keep your feet steady, shoulders relaxed and elbows near your torso.

Bend your elbows to curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders without rocking your torso. Keep your upper arms mostly still, then lower the weights under control until your arms are extended comfortably.
Stand facing the cable with the attachment set around chest height. Hold it with both hands, elbows bent and close to your sides. Set your feet securely and keep your torso steady.

Straighten your elbows to press the attachment down while keeping your upper arms near your sides. Finish in a comfortable extension, then bend your elbows slowly to return. Avoid leaning your body onto the handle.
Stand on a level floor with a dumbbell in each hand beside your thighs. Set your feet about hip width apart and keep your knees softly extended. Choose a load that lets you balance without rocking.

Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels while keeping your torso steady. Pause briefly, then lower your heels to the floor under control. Keep the dumbbells beside your body and avoid bouncing.

Adjust the standing calf raise machine so the shoulder pads rest comfortably on your shoulders. Select or rack the load according to the machine, then stand with the balls of your feet on its platform and hold the handles. Lift into a steady position and release the safety catch if present.

Raise your heels by pressing through the balls of your feet, keeping your knees softly extended and your torso steady. Pause briefly, then lower your heels through a comfortable range without bouncing. Re-engage the safety catch if present before stepping off.
Hold a pull-up bar with a secure, comfortable grip and let your body hang without swinging. Keep your shoulders controlled and legs together, with knees straight or softly bent as needed.

Lift your legs by bringing your thighs toward your torso without building momentum. Raise only through a range you can control, then lower slowly until your body is still. Bend your knees if that helps maintain control.

Practise the setup with a load you can control before increasing it. Keep the bar close, establish a steady trunk position before lifting, and reset between repetitions rather than rushing the next pull.
Practise the hip hinge before adding heavier load. Keep the bar close and stop the descent before you lose control of your trunk position; reaching the floor is not the goal.
Practise the hip hinge with light dumbbells first. Keep them close to your legs and limit the descent to the range you can control; do not reach lower by changing your trunk position.
Technique considerations
Set an adjustable bench to a low incline and sit with a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs. Lie back and bring the dumbbells beside your upper chest, feet planted and upper back supported.
Press both dumbbells up over your upper chest, keeping your wrists steady. Lower them under control until your elbows are beside your torso, then press again without clashing the weights.
Place your hands on a bench, step or low platform a little wider than shoulder width and extend your legs behind you. Brace your trunk so your head, hips and legs stay in one line.
Lower your chest toward the raised support by bending your elbows, keeping your body straight. Press back up until your arms are extended. A higher support makes the movement easier.
Set both cable pulleys around chest height and take a handle in each hand. Stand a step forward with one foot slightly ahead, elbows softly bent, and let your arms open to the sides.
Bring the handles toward each other in front of your chest in a wide arc, keeping your elbows softly bent. Squeeze briefly, then let your arms open under control until you feel a comfortable stretch.
Anchor a resistance band behind you at chest height and hold one end in each hand beside your chest. Stand with a stable stance and keep your shoulders settled.
Press your hands forward until your arms are extended, keeping the band under tension. Return slowly until your hands are beside your chest without letting the band snap back.

Grip parallel bars and lift yourself to a supported position with your arms extended. Keep your shoulders settled down away from your ears and your legs under control. Use an assisted dip machine or band if bodyweight is too much.

Bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms are around horizontal or a comfortable depth. Press back up until your arms are extended. Keep the descent controlled rather than dropping into it.
Stand with your feet about hip width apart holding a barbell with an overhand grip. Hinge at your hips until your torso is inclined, keep a steady trunk, and let the bar hang below your shoulders.
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs by driving your elbows back, keeping your torso angle steady. Lower the bar under control until your arms are extended. Avoid jerking the bar with your lower back.
Reach up and grip a pull-up bar with your hands a little wider than shoulder width, palms facing away. Hang with your arms extended and shoulders controlled, legs together or softly bent.

Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down until your chin approaches the bar, or as high as you can control. Lower slowly to a full hang without swinging. Use assistance if you cannot control the descent.
Grip a pull-up bar with your palms facing you and your hands about shoulder width apart. Hang with your arms extended and your shoulders settled, keeping your body still.
Pull yourself upward until your chin nears the bar, keeping your elbows moving down and back. Lower under control to a full hang. Add assistance if the movement is not yet controllable.
Anchor a resistance band at waist or chest height and hold one end in each hand. Step back until the band is under light tension, soften your knees and keep your trunk steady.
Pull your hands toward your ribs by driving your elbows back, keeping your shoulders down. Return slowly until your arms are extended and the band is still taut.
Hold a light resistance band in front of you with both hands about shoulder width apart and your arms extended. Stand tall with your ribs down and your shoulders relaxed.

Open your arms by pulling the band apart until it nears your chest, keeping your elbows softly bent. Return slowly to the start without letting the band snap. Use a lighter band rather than shrugging.
Sit or stand with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward or slightly inward. Keep your trunk steady and your upper back supported if seated.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are extended, without clashing them overhead. Lower under control until your elbows are around shoulder height or a comfortable depth.

Set a cable pulley low and hold the handle with the hand furthest from the machine, or use a light single-hand setting. Stand side-on with the cable crossing in front of your body and a soft elbow bend.
Raise your arm out to the side until it is around shoulder height, leading with your elbow. Lower under control to the start. Keep the movement smooth rather than swinging the weight up.
Set a cable pulley around face height and attach a rope. Hold one end in each hand with your thumbs pointing back, arms extended, and stand with a stable stance.

Pull the rope toward your face by driving your elbows out and back, finishing with your hands beside your head. Return under control until your arms are extended. Use a load that lets you keep your shoulders relaxed.
Stand upright holding a barbell with an underhand grip about shoulder width apart. Keep your elbows near your sides and your trunk steady.
Bend your elbows to curl the bar toward your chest without swinging your torso. Lower the bar under control until your arms are extended. Keep your wrists in line with your forearms.
Stand on the middle of a resistance band or anchor it low, and hold one end in each hand with your palms facing up. Keep your elbows beside your torso and stand tall.
Curl your hands toward your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still. Lower slowly against the band's tension until your arms are extended.
Hold a single dumbbell with both hands, or one dumbbell in each hand, and raise it overhead with your arms extended. Keep your elbows pointing forward and your trunk steady.
Bend your elbows to lower the weight behind your head through a comfortable range. Straighten your elbows to return overhead. Keep your upper arms from drifting outward.
Lie on the bench and grip the bar with your hands about shoulder width apart. Settle your upper back, plant your feet, and unrack with your arms extended.
Lower the bar toward your lower chest with your elbows close to your torso. Touch lightly, then press up until your arms are extended. Keep your wrists steady over your forearms.

Rest the bar across the front of your shoulders with your elbows high and your hands outside your shoulders, or use a crossed-arm grip. Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and brace your trunk.
Squat down by bending your knees and hips while keeping your torso upright and your elbows lifted. Descend to a comfortable depth, then drive up through your feet to standing.
Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and your toes pointing slightly out. Keep your arms in front of you or at your sides for balance and brace your trunk.
Bend your knees and hips to sit down and back while keeping your heels down. Descend to a comfortable depth, then stand up and finish tall. Use a chair or support if you need help with balance.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Stand about a stride in front of a bench and place one foot on it behind you with your toes down. Set your front foot flat and keep your torso steady.

Bend your front knee and hip to lower your body, keeping your front heel down and your torso upright. Descend to a comfortable depth, then drive up through your front foot. Use a lower support if balance is difficult.
